newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine mining stocks reel on Busang gold fears.
newsitem.headline: Philippine mining stocks reel on Busang gold fears.

text.p: Philippine mining stocks posted losses on Monday as doubts over reserves of the Busang gold find in Indonesia dampened investor sentiment, but analysts said the sector's selloff should be short-lived.
The mining sub-index closed 591.64 points lower, or 9.34 percent, to 5,743.85 points.

Within the group, Lepanto Consolidated Mining Co B shares shed 17.65 percent to 1.12 peso while A shares dipped 8.24 percent to 78 centavos. United Paragon Mining Corp shares settled 12 percent lower at 2.20 centavos.

"Investors felt that if doubts were raised on Busang, said to be the biggest gold discovery in the world, then it could happen to less significant mining sites," said Jonas Ferrer, vice-president at Pryce Securities.

"It probably dawned on investors here that in mining, what is expected to be there, may not be there at all. The Busang incident was a reality check for investors dabbling in speculative stocks," said Helen Alvarez, research head at All Asia Securties.
Bre-X Minerals Ltd initially said its Busang find deep in the jungles of Indonesia's Borneo island contained about 71 million ounces of gold worth $25 billion at current prices.
It was touted as the biggest single gold find this century.

But Bre-X chief executive David Walsh said in a statement last week that "there appears a strong possibility" that the potential gold resources had been "overstated". Walsh later said the company remains confident of Busang's reserve potential.
Despite the assurance, investors were still skeptical, sending Bre-X stock price lower.
Ferrer said the negative sentiment exacerbated by a dearth of any fresh compelling news caused Philippine mining stocks to regress.
Still, analysts and the Chamber of Mines said the stock losses will not run deep and would be short-lived.

"There is no cause to panic. We are far away from what happened and most mining companies here are operating ones and are familiar with their terrain, a big difference from Busang which has yet to begin production," said Artemio F. Disini, president of the Chamber of Mines and Lepanto Consolidated Mining Co.
Disini said the Philippine mining industry remained attractive despite the Marcopper Mining Corp accident last year where tonnes of waste from a mine run by Marcopper leaked into a nearby river.
On the spill-over effects of the Busang find, he said: "This will all settle down."
Disini said the passage of the Mining Law in 1995 which allowed foreign firms 100 percent stake in local mining projects had kept interest alive in the mining industry.
Big mining companies such as Barrick Gold Corp, and WMC Ltd have expressed interest in the sector, he said.
WMC and Arimco of Australia have already been granted financial and technical assistance agreements (FTAAs).

"Release of first quarter earnings results of mining firms will give investors more direction. This is probably just a temporary setback for the industry," said April Bautista, analyst at Anscor-Hagedorn Securities Inc.
